gifts.title: A working website, since yours doesn't load at all
gifts.for_complaint: No way to check if they're actually open / hours unclear + site is dead + not on OpenStreetMap
gifts.deliverable: A one-page site at a URL: address, phone, real hours, an embedded map, and a 'Find Your Stylist' section naming Justin, Nikki Yates, Danni, Melodie, Molly, Cami with their specialty pulled straight from real reviews — replacing the URLError page entirely.
gifts.inputs_needed: Current hours and phone (site is down, so these must come from the public Google Business listing, not the salon's own domain); address is already public (916 E Douglas Ave). No login or contact required — Google's public listing page is fetchable without authentication.
gifts.why_they_stop_and_read: Right now a customer who Googles J. Gilman Salon hits a dead link — this is the first thing that's been at that URL in who knows how long, built from their own 171 five-star reviews.

gifts.title: Find Your Stylist, so people stop guessing
gifts.for_complaint: Hard to know which stylist to pick without already knowing a name
gifts.deliverable: A one-screen stylist directory page: photo-less profile cards for each named stylist (Justin — color & transformations, Nikki Yates — color correction & kids, Danni — major color work & long sessions, Melodie — communicative multi-visit plans, Molly — classic cuts), each with 1-2 real client quotes as proof, and a 'call to book with them' line.
gifts.inputs_needed: Nothing beyond the reviews already supplied — no menu, hours, or map required for this piece alone. Fully buildable from what's on hand.
gifts.why_they_stop_and_read: Six different reviewers describe the same struggle — moving to a new city, not knowing who to trust — right before naming the exact stylist who fixed it. This page is that answer, indexed.

gifts.title: Our Fix-It Promise, printed at checkout
gifts.for_complaint: Charged full price (or more) to fix their own mistake + botched cut/color with no fix
gifts.deliverable: A single printable card for the front desk/checkout counter: a plain-language service-recovery promise ('If it's not right, we make it right — free, within 7 days') with a short claim line for the client to fill in, directly answering the three reviews that describe being asked to pay again to fix a mistake.
gifts.inputs_needed: None — this is a policy card, not data-dependent. It's a draft for the owner to adopt or edit, not something requiring their systems.
gifts.why_they_stop_and_read: Every 1-star review that mentions money is the same shape: 'they wanted me to pay more to fix it.' This is the one page that could have turned three of those into a 5-star instead.
